paper_metadata.title: A New Algorithm for Applying Sequences of Affine Transformations in Quantum Circuits

summary: The paper proposes a gate-based method for sequential affine transformations in quantum circuits using block encoding and Hadamard-supported conditional initialization. It reports a 4-qubit resource comparison showing 213 total gates for the proposed approach versus 313 for a block-encoded augmented-matrix method, and illustrates two applications: a conceptual portfolio-return construction and a 10-qubit QFT-affine-IQFT signal-processing example.

experiments.description: Gate-based quantum circuit experiment demonstrating sequential affine transformations on a 4-qubit system and comparing gate counts against a block-encoded augmented-matrix approach.

algorithm.variant: Sequential affine transformations using block encoding and Hadamard-supported conditional initialization
algorithm.parameter_initialization: normalized input state initialization; conditional initialization of translation vectors

problem_formulation.encoding_details: A 4x4 matrix A is embedded into an 8x8 unitary U1; translation vector B is incorporated via Hadamard-supported add/sub on an expanded register
problem_formulation.objective_function: Apply a sequence of affine transformations of the form A_k ... A_2 A_1 Ψ + B_1 + B_2 + ... in amplitude space
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Normalization preserved via block encoding and Hadamard-supported conditional initialization

problem_instance.description: Toy 4-qubit affine-transformation circuit used to compare resource counts between the proposed method and an augmented-matrix block-encoding method
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Normalized input state; translation vector zero-padded/rescaled as needed

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: State initialization and zero-padding/rescaling of translation vectors
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measurement-based recovery of scaled affine outputs; classical rescaling by known factors

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports a gate-count reduction only for a toy 4-qubit example; it does not establish asymptotic speedup or hardware performance.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: 4-qubit toy circuit; 213 total gates for the proposed method versus 313 for the block-encoded augmented-matrix method
limiting_factors: Only a small 4-qubit example is reported
No runtime, shot count, or hardware execution is provided

notes: Hardware inferred as simulator_other because the paper reports Qiskit circuit implementation and gate counts but no real QPU/device execution.
The paper reports gate counts for a 4-qubit system (93 single-qubit + 120 multi-qubit = 213 total) and compares decomposed circuits; no transpiled depth or shot count is given.
No asymptotic speedup is established; the paper only reports a 32% gate-count reduction for the toy example.
The paper reports a 32% reduction in total gate count (213 vs 313) for a 4-qubit example, but this is not a demonstrated practical advantage.

experiments.description: Financial risk assessment / portfolio-return demonstration using successive Hadamard-supported add/sub operations on a normalized portfolio vector.

algorithm.parameter_initialization: normalized portfolio list encoded into amplitudes

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Portfolio values are encoded into amplitudes; each step appends one qubit and applies Hadamard-supported add/sub with the next block of assets
problem_formulation.objective_function: Compute combinatorial portfolio-return amplitudes F(i0,...,im-1) from signed sums of asset values
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Normalization preserved by scaling each add/sub step by 1/2; measurement/post-selection on bitstrings

problem_instance.description: Illustrative portfolio-return example; no concrete market dataset or ticker list is provided

dataset_specification.description: Normalized portfolio list P; assets grouped by importance; no real-market data specified

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Assets sorted so ai >= ai+1; initial state normalized; successive blocks Bk formed from next 2^k assets
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Analytical derivation of output amplitudes; no numerical benchmark or repeated-run statistics reported

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Sorting portfolio assets and forming successive blocks Bk
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Estimate amplitudes from repeated measurements; interpret highest-probability bitstrings as largest combinatorial returns

speedup_claims.caveats: No classical baseline, runtime, or empirical performance comparison is reported for the portfolio-return construction.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: No concrete qubit count, depth, runtime, or benchmarked classical baseline is reported for the portfolio-return construction
limiting_factors: No hardware or simulator run reported

notes: The paper describes the portfolio-return construction conceptually and does not report a concrete hardware run, qubit count, or depth for this application.
Qiskit is mentioned in the paper generally, but no specific device or execution setup is given for the portfolio example.
No asymptotic speedup is claimed; the method is presented as a combinatorial amplitude construction.
The portfolio example is presented as an illustrative application with analytical amplitude formulas, not as a benchmarked experiment.

experiments.description: Discrete signal-processing demonstration: QFT on an input signal, one affine transformation in Fourier space, then inverse QFT to return to the time domain.

algorithm.variant: QFT -> affine transformation -> inverse QFT signal manipulation

hyperparameters.signal_model: xn = sum_i A_i sin(2π f_i t_n)

algorithm.parameter_initialization: signal amplitudes A_i encoded into a quantum state

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Signal amplitudes A_i are encoded as amplitudes of a quantum state; QFT acts on the encoded signal, followed by affine modification in Fourier space
problem_formulation.objective_function: Modify Fourier coefficients via X~_k = a X_k + b and reconstruct the time-domain signal with inverse QFT
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Normalization handled implicitly by quantum state preparation and affine scaling
